en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Garlic Chapter.
4. The Training Rule on Bone-Dust.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain former royal concubine had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs.
A certain bhikkhunī, oppressed by lack of spiritual delight, approached that bhikkhunī and said to her:
"Venerable lady, the king does not visit you from time to time."
“How do you maintain it?
“By means of a wax plug, venerable lady.
“What is this ‘wax plug,’ venerable lady?”
Then that nun told the other nun about the wax-sealing device.
Having taken the wax-sealing device, that nun forgot to wash it and threw it away to one side.
When the nuns saw it surrounded by flies, they said this:
“Whose deed is this?
She replied, “It is my deed.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before] ...were indignant, disparaged it, and complained about it.
“How indeed could a bhikkhunī take up a wax-seal?
… [as before] … “Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī takes up a wax-seal?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can a bhikkhunī apply collyrium mixed with beeswax?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without confidence nor for the increase of the confidence of those who have it…” [and so on].
And thus, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:
"In the case of a dildo, there is an offense entailing expiation.
A dildo means:
Made of lac, made of wood, made of flour, or made of clay.
"Should take" means:
if, relishing the contact, she inserts even a lotus leaf into the urinary organ, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense:
if it is due to illness,
or if she is insane.
"Regarding the first offender":
thus ends the fourth training rule.
